implementation_notes: Rust absorbs the pattern: traits are the abstraction, generics with trait bounds give zero-cost static dispatch, `dyn Trait` gives runtime dispatch when the implementation must be chosen at run time, and sealed traits (a private supertrait) close a hierarchy. Dependency inversion is just passing `impl Trait` parameters. The one place SOLID needs translating is that LSP violations become compile errors at every call site.
idiom_name: trait + generic bound (static) or dyn trait (dynamic)
pitfalls: Trait objects erase generics and require `dyn`; mixing generic and dyn versions of the same API duplicates surface area.
The orphan rule blocks implementing a foreign trait for a foreign type, which can force an awkward newtype wrapper.
Async traits with `async fn` in traits (stable since 1.75) still need `Send` bounds propagated explicitly.
Sealing a trait you do not own is impossible — vendoring becomes the only way to close the hierarchy.
